title: The Language of Experts
text:
Every specialized field relies on a vocabulary that outsiders find opaque. Surgeons speak of anastomosis, lawyers invoke estoppel, and economists refer to quantitative easing without pausing to explain. Such jargon is not merely decorative; it compresses complex ideas into terms that practitioners can use with precision. Yet the same density can exclude newcomers who lack the shared background.

Mastering jargon therefore involves more than memorising definitions. A learner must recognise when a term carries a narrow technical meaning and when it has drifted into everyday speech. Experts often switch registers depending on their audience, simplifying their language for patients or clients. Recognising that switch is itself a sign of fluency.

questions.text: According to the passage, what do economists refer to without pausing to explain?
According to the passage, what must a learner be able to recognise?
options: when a term carries a narrow technical meaning
how to invent new technical terms
the origin of every legal term

questions.text: Why might dense jargon exclude some people, according to the passage?
options: They lack the shared background needed to follow it
They are unable to read any written text
Experts never use it in conversation

questions.text: What does the passage imply about experts who simplify their language?
options: They do not understand their own field
They adjust their register to suit their audience
They use jargon only with other experts

vocabulary.definition: not clear or easy to understand
the quality of being exact and accurate
the ability to use a language or skill smoothly and easily

paragraph_translations: Todo campo especializado depende de un vocabulario que resulta opaco para quienes están fuera. Los cirujanos hablan de anastomosis, los abogados invocan la estoppel y los economistas se refieren a la flexibilización cuantitativa sin detenerse a explicarla. Esta jerga no es solo decorativa; condensa ideas complejas en términos que los profesionales pueden usar con precisión. Sin embargo, esa misma densidad puede excluir a los recién llegados que carecen del conocimiento compartido.

Dominar la jerga, por tanto, implica más que memorizar definiciones. Un estudiante debe reconocer cuándo un término tiene un significado técnico restringido y cuándo ha pasado al lenguaje cotidiano. Los expertos suelen cambiar de registro según su público, simplificando su lenguaje para pacientes o clientes. Reconocer ese cambio es en sí mismo una señal de fluidez.
